stepBody:
Now suppose we fit two linear models on the humans data.
Model A:
$$\hat{b}=	heta_0+	heta_{in}h_{in}+	heta_{cm}h_{cm}+	heta_{lb}w_{lb}+	heta_{kg}w_{kg}$$
Model B:
$$\hat{b}= eta_0+ eta_{cm}h_{cm}+ eta_{kg}w_{kg}$$
Here $$\hat{b}$$ is predicted bmi, $$h_{in}$$ and $$h_{cm}$$ are height in inches and centimeters, and $$w_{lb}$$ and $$w_{kg}$$ are weight in pounds and kilograms.
Suppose we create 95% confidence intervals for each of these non-intercept parameters using the bootstrap method. Are the parameters' confidence interval likely to contain the value 0? Select all that apply.
